takeaway: Facial pain over the upper and lower jaws, set off by washing, shaving, eating or a cold wind, is trigeminal neuralgia: pain in the sensory distribution of the trigeminal nerve.

lines.text: A 50-year-old man has recent onset of pain in his face.
lines.say: A fifty-year-old man has recent onset of pain in his face.

lines.text: The pain lies over his upper and lower jaws.
Washing his face sets off the pain.
Shaving brings on the same pain.
Eating brings it on as well.
Even a cold wind blowing on his face can trigger it.
This is trigeminal neuralgia, pain in the sensory distribution of the trigeminal nerve.
So the nerve causing his symptoms is the trigeminal nerve.
